A. PRADHAN MANTRI KAUSHAL VIKAS YOJANA (PMKVY4.0)  
28.  MSDE is implementing its flagship scheme Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas 
Yojana (PMKVY), since 2015, for imparting skill development training through 
Short-Term Training (STT) and up-skilling and re-skilling through Recognition of 
Prior Learning (RPL) to youth across the country. It aims to stimulate and 
advance skill development across the country by delivering high-quality, short-
duration training programs in job roles as per the industry requirements. Since 
its inception, three iterations of PMKVY have been successfully implemented, with 
the current phase, PMKVY 4.0, underway. As on 09.01.2025, more than 1.60 
crore candidates have been trained under the PMKVY.  
 
29.  PMKVY 4.0 (2022-26) has been designed with various new elements 
including On-the-job training (OJT), Integration and mainstreaming of vocational 
education with general education as per ‘National Education Policy’ (NEP) 2020, 
offering training in futuristic and new age courses for Industrial Revolution 4.0, 
expanding the delivery network for skill development through cross utilization of 
resources by setting Skill India Centres (SICs) in Institutes of National Repute, 
Schools, Colleges, Universities, Technical Institutions, etc. Under PMKVY 4.0, 
training is being imparted in Short-Term Training (STT), Recognition of Prior 
Learning (RPL) and Special Projects (SP). 
 
The broad design principles of PMKVY 4.0 are: 
 
i. Customized courses with high employability and duration up-to 210 hours. 
ii. Short-Term Training (STT) are by educational institutions (Colleges, 
Schools and Government Institutions), including ITIs to synergize 
vocational and educational streams and increase network of quality 
training providers by increasing partnership of educational and vocational 
institutions. 
iii. Skill courses are selected as per Industry demand. 
iv. Special Projects for identified areas and groups in agriculture, handicraft 
and other traditional sectors. 
v. Skill India Digital Hub (SIDH) platform has been launched for capturing the 
entire training lifecycle. 
vi. Enhanced industry-connect through greater reliance on On-the-Job 
Training in short-term training.  

 
16 
 
vii. Emphasis on re-skilling, and up-skilling under Recognition of Prior 
Learning (RPL) through innovation in assessment and better monitoring. 
viii. Simplified procedures for reducing compliance burden by enlisting multiple 
Assessment Agencies and Awarding Bodies, re-engineering IT systems 
based on requirement of stakeholders, etc. 
ix. Creation of a national pool of trainers and assessors to ensure their 
availability and efficient implementation of training and faster assessment. 
x. Flexibility in course curriculum by introducing courses in partnership with 
industry, other Ministries/Departments, etc. 
xi. Focus on online/digital/blended skilling for effective learning, convenience, 
and outreach. 
xii. Emphasis on community engagement through training in job roles 
addressing the skill needs of the informal sector or basic self-employed. 
xiii. Focus on New Age Skills like Industry 4.0, Web 3.0, AI/ML, AR/VR, 
Climate Change, Circular Economy, Green Economy, and Energy 
Transition.

40. The Committee desired to know as to how the Ministry monitor functioning 
of Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Kendras (PMKKs) and the details of number of 
inspections undertaken during the last three years, deficiencies noticed and steps 
taken to improve their functioning. In reply, the Ministry stated as follow:-      
              
“A robust monitoring framework has been put in place under the Pradhan 
Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana (PMKVY) 4.0 scheme to ensure strict monitoring. To 
monitor the effectiveness of the skill training provided under PMKVY, the Ministry 
has launched Skill India Digital Hub (SIDH), a unified platform that integrates 
skilling, education, employment, and entrepreneurship ecosystems to provide a 
life-long array of services targeting a wide range of stakeholders.  
 
Further, the following steps are undertaken to ensure quality standards 
across all training centres, including PMKKs, while imparting training under 
PMKVY 4.0:- 
  
i. The registration process on SIDH ensures e-KYC compliance, Aadhaar based 
authentication of candidate credentials, and mobile number authentication. 
ii. Mandatory Aadhar Enabled Biometric Attendance System (AEBAS). 
iii. Virtual verification of operational training centres using a mobile app, monitor 
remote Training Centres (TCs) locations virtually at any given point of time. 
iv. Call validations are carried out on regular basis for taking feedback of 
candidates on their experiences and support investigation process in case of 
grievances received against Training Partners/Centres. 
v. Physical visits and inspection of the training centre by officials from MSDE and 
State Engagement Officers / other representatives from NSDC are regularly 
undertaken. 
vi. Virtual monitoring through audio and video calls is also conducted by a 
Kaushal Samiksha Kendra set up in MSDE. 
  
Over the last 3 years,a total of 637 Physical Inspections (PIs) have been 
undertaken. The key deficiencies observed during these inspections include non-
conduct of training during visits, PMKKs being closed on working days, non-
compliance with equipment guidelines, candidates being unavailable during visits, 
batch merging, low attendance (below 50%), mismatches between physical 
attendance and AEBAS records, and in some cases, PMKKs not being found at the 
registered address on SIDH.  
          
PMKKs with severe discrepancies are issued Show Cause Notices and 
undergo a Consequence Management process, with penal actions such as 
suspension, financial penalties, and batch cancellations imposed on non-
compliant centres. In order to avoid further occurrence of such discrepancies, 
workshops are also conducted to orient PMKKs on quality delivery of training, 
retention of candidates post mobilization, maintenance of attendance etc.”

B.  JAN SHIKSHAN SANSTHAN (JSS)  
53. The scheme of Jan Shikshan Sansthan  (JSS), initially launched in 1967 as 
Shramik Vidyapeeth (SVP), aims to provide skill development training in a non-

 
31 
 
formal mode at the doorsteps of the beneficiary through registered Societies 
(NGOs) with 100% grant from the Government of India. The objective of the 
scheme is to increase household income by promoting self/wage employment 
through skill development training.  The skill training is low-cost, flexible, and 
highly accessible to Women, Scheduled Caste (SC), Scheduled Tribe (ST), Other 
Backward Classes (OBCs), minorities, and any other disadvantaged groups of 
society. 
 
54. The target beneficiaries of the scheme are non-literate, neo-literate and the 
person having a rudimentary level of education (70%), school dropouts up to class 
12th (20%), and graduates (10%) in the age group of 15-45 years. Age relaxation 
is given to Divyang and other deserving cases, especially women. The priority 
groups are Women, SC, ST, OBCs and minorities in rural areas and urban low-
income areas.  
 
55 The scheme is implemented through JSSs, functioning under the aegis of 
respective parent bodies. The parent body should register the JSS as a separate 
NGO under the Societies Registration Act, 1860. These JSSs receive financial 
assistance in the form of Grants-in-Aid (GIA) from the Government of India for 
imparting skill training to the assigned target.

65.   When asked to provide the details of specific vocational training and skill 
development initiatives that are being implemented under JSS Scheme and the 
manner in which these initiatives address the needs of marginalized 
communities, the Ministry submitted as follows:-  
“The Jan Shikshan Sansthan (JSS) Scheme, initially launched as Shramik 
Vidyapeeth (SVP) in 1967, aims to provide skill training in a non-formal mode at the 
doorsteps of the beneficiary through registered Societies (NGOs) with 100% grant 
from the Government of India. The objective of the scheme is to increase the 
household income by promoting self/wage employment through skill development 
training. The skill training provided through JSSs is, flexible, affordable and highly 
accessible to women, Scheduled Castes (SC), Scheduled Tribes (ST), Other 
Backward Classes (OBCs), minorities, and any other disadvantaged groups of 
society. The target beneficiaries of the scheme are non-literates, neo-literates and 
persons having rudimentary level of education, school dropouts up to class 12th in 
the age group of 15-45 years. Age relaxation is given to Divyangjan and other 
deserving cases, especially women.  
  The following vocational training and skill development initiatives are being 
implemented under the JSS Scheme to address the needs of JSS beneficiaries, 
including marginalized communities: 
Livelihood Cell: Each JSS has a livelihood cell that connects JSS beneficiaries to 
employment, develops entrepreneurship skills, facilitates SHG formation, provides 
credit linkages, etc. 
Creation of Model JSS:Training infrastructure of 30 JSS centers has been 
upgraded for 3 identified job roles Assistant Computer Operator, Assistant Dress 

 
43 
 
Maker, and Beauty Care Assistant under SANKALP project of MSDE. Further, the 
upgradation of 70 more JSSs as Model JSSs is under process. 
Onboarding to SIDH Portal: JSS data has been migrated to the Skill India Digital 
Hub (SIDH) portal, ensuring mobile OTP-based candidate enrollment and 
Aadhaar-based e-KYC for transparency in candidate onboarding and training 
within the JSS ecosystem. 
 
NCVET certification: As the JSS Scheme has been onboarded to SIDH portal, 
from FY 2024-25 onwards, the JSS beneficiaries are now being issued NCVET 
certificate, which consists of QR Code, Credits earned, Beneficiary photo, NSQF 
level, etc. This has enhanced the credibility of JSS certification. 
Courses: 13 new-age NSQF-aligned courses (Level 2/3) have been adopted in the 
FY 2024-25, after approval from the National Council for Vocational Education 
and Training (NCVET). 
Convergence:  JSS scheme has been converged with schemes such as PM 
Vishwakarma Scheme, ULLAS scheme of MoE, Pradhan Mantri Janjati Adivasi 
Nyaya Maha Abhiyan (PM JANMAN) , Pradhan Mantri Janjatiya Unnat Gram 
Abhiyan (PM JUGA) etc 
Capacity Building: Ministry has organized zonal workshops at various locations 
and various capacity-building activities with stakeholders such as the National 
Institute for Entrepreneurship and Small Business Development (NIESBUD), the 
Institute of Rural Management, Anand (IRMA), etc, for capacity building of the 
JSSs in the areas such as Linkage with Entrepreneurship, Social Media presence 
and advocacy, Strengthening of Livelihood cells, etc. 
 
Simplifying the Board of Management creation in the JSSs: The affairs of each 
Jan ShikshanSansthan (JSS) are to be managed by a Board of Management that 
represents the interest of the target beneficiaries. JSS has its BoM which acts as 
an administrative body to supervise the functioning of the JSS.  
In order to strengthen the Board of the Management of the JSSs, the 
Ministry has undertaken the following initiatives: - 
- Providing Designation based Government nominations for the 
representatives in the BoM. 
- RDSDE as nominee of the Joint Secretary in the Board of Management of 
the JSSs 
Monitoring: To ensure effective on-ground implementation, the JSS scheme is 
monitored through the SIDH portal and field visits by MSDE and RDSDE officials. 
Udhyam Kart: As a step toward providing a platform to showcase and sell 
products made by JSS beneficiaries and to empower budding entrepreneurs under 
JSS Scheme, a dedicated section for JSS products has been successfully created 
on the UdhyamKart portal, developed by NIESBUD.” 
 
66.  On being asked about the details of measures taken to assess the 
effectiveness of the JSSs programmes in improving the employability and income-
generating capacity of its beneficiaries, the Ministry stated as under:-       
“In order to assess the effectiveness of the JSSs programmes in improving the 
employability and income-generating capacity of its beneficiaries an evaluation 

 
44 
 
study was conducted by Indian Institute of Public Administration (IIPA) in FY 
2020-21.   
Considering 79% women representation, 50.5% of the rural share, 73.4% change 
in the employment for enhanced livelihood, 89.1% change in the average income of 
each beneficiary, 85.7% mobilization of beneficiaries by JSS, the study team 
recommended the scheme of Jan Shikshan  Sansthan for continuation.” 
 
67. The progress of the JSS Scheme is monitored through the JSS portal and 
the same is being migrated to the new Skill India Digital Hub (SIDH) Portal. When 
asked about the present status and the time by when the exercise is proposed to 
be completed, the Ministry stated as follows:-                                                   
 
  “In order to bring convergence among various skilling efforts across the 
nation, the Skill India Digital Hub (SIDH) is specially designed and developed by 
the Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE).  
  From present Financial year onwards, with the approval of the Competent 
Authority, the skill training under the JSS scheme has been successfully 
operational on SIDH portal. This means that entire training life cycle of the 
beneficiary i.e. Enrolment, Batch creation, training, Assessment and Certification 
(NCVET certification) is being carried out on SIDH portal. Migration to SIDH portal 
has ensured Mobile OTP-based candidate enrolment and Aadhar based e-KYC 
ensuring transparency in candidate onboarding and training in the JSS 
Ecosystem. Major monitoring modules under the JSS scheme such as Annual 
Action Plan, Board of Management etc has also been made functional on SIDH. 
The detailed JSS wise data analytics has also been made in form of the Live 
Dashboard on SIDH portal. 
Presently, the existing JSS portal (www.jss.gov.in) is in the last stage of 
migration into the SIDH portal. It is expected that the migration process will be 
completed by March 2025. This migration will strengthen the JSS ecosystem and 
the JSS beneficiaries will also be able to utilize various other benefits of the 
portal.”  
  
C.  NATIONAL APPRENTICESHIP PROMOTION SCHEME (NAPS) - New Version 
 
68. National Apprenticeship Promotion Scheme (NAPS) aims to promote 
apprenticeship training in the country, by providing partial stipend support to the 
apprentices engaged under the Apprentices Act, 1961 and rules thereby. National 
Apprenticeship Promotion Scheme (NAPS) launched in August 2016 and 
continues as NAPS-2 since 2022-23. Starting August 2023, Direct Benefit 
Transfer (DBT) was launched under NAPS-2. Partial stipend support by GoI 
under NAPS-2 limited to 25% of stipend paid, up to a maximum of Rs.1,500 per 
month, per apprentice is provided during the training period. The stipend support 
by GoI is paid through Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) to the bank account of 
apprentices.

candidates dropped out in 2022-23, 2.37 lakh in 2023-24 and 2.89 lakh in 2024-
25 i.e. there is persistent increase in the candidates who dropped out during the 
last three years. When enquired about   the road map to minimize the dropouts 
under the Scheme, the Ministry in their subsequent written reply stated as 
under:-     
           
“Since apprenticeship training happens within an establishment, significant 
challenges faced by a person during the apprenticeship training includes 
relocation challenges from place of living to establishment location at new 
location, factory/ industry/ establishment environment, cost of living, 
environmental conditions, health etc. Attractive, alternative options also lead to 
dropout in apprenticeship training. 
Workshops/ awareness programme on apprenticeship training are being 
organized to sensitize various stake holders on apprenticeship training. Further, 
Pradhan Mantri National Apprenticeship Mela (PMNAM) facilitates as a platform to 
disseminate information on apprenticeship training. Efforts will be also made for a 
supportive workplace culture by establishments. States/ UTs will be sensitized to 
make use of PMNAM / workshops/ awareness programme to disseminate 
information for assisting interested persons to take informed decisions before 
joining the apprenticeship training.This is expected to support reducing the 
dropout numbers under apprenticeship training. Further, revision to the 
minimum stipend rate to the apprentices is also being explored that is expectedto 
make the apprenticeship training programme attractive.”

asked to provide the  reasons for consistent shortfall in actual expenditure during 
the last three financial years, the Ministry stated as under:-                                      
“The North Eastern Region (NER) is provided with gross budgetary support 
amounting to at least 10% of the allocation of schemes. If the scheme expenditure 
is low for any reason, it correspondingly impacts the NER's expenditure. For 
example, due to the non-approval of funds for the ‘Skill India Programme,’ 
anticipated funds could not be released, which also affected the disbursements for 
the NER states. Additionally, fund releases under various Ministry schemes are 
demand-driven; thus, funds are only disbursed upon receiving demands from 
states that meet the mandatory conditions prescribed in the SNA/CNA guidelines, 
such as utilizing 75% of previous allocations. States that request funds and comply 
with the release conditions are granted funds promptly.”

D.  NATIONAL SCHEME FOR ITIs UPGRADATION  
93. Announced in budget 2024-25, Scheme for upgradation of ITIs aims to 
enhance the quality and outcomes of skilling across India by upgrading 1,000 ITIs 
in a hub-and-spoke arrangement over five years. It will be a new Centrally 
Sponsored Scheme, with a total outlay of Rs.60,000 crore, with contributions 
from the Government of India (Rs.30,000 crore), State Governments (Rs. 20,000 
crore), and the industry, including CSR funding (Rs.10,000 crore). 
 
94. It will involve upgradation of 200 hubs and 800 spoke ITIs, all working 
closely with industry partners to redesign existing courses, introduce new 
courses, along with specialized short-term courses. Additionally, the programme 
includes capacity augmentation of five national institutes for training trainers. 
With these initiatives, it is expected to benefit 20 lakh students over the course of 
five years. A demand of  Rs.5010 crore was placed for FY.2025-26. However 
considering that the scheme is yet at the initial stage, the Ministry of Finance 
agreed for an allocation of Rs.3000.00 crore, for FY.2025-26. 
 
95. It was noticed that for the FY 2025-26, the Gross Demand for Grants for the 
Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship is Rs. 8300.10 Cr and the 
net demand is Rs.6100.10 Cr. The demand of Rs. 6100.10 Cr also includes Rs. 
3000.00 Cr for the ‘New ITI Upgradation Scheme’, which is yet to be approved by 
the Cabinet.  The Committee desired to know about the present status of the 
implementation of the Scheme and how the funds earmarked are proposed to be 
utilized during the current fiscal. In response, the Ministry apprised as under:-    
 
“The ‘National Scheme for ITIs Upgradation’ has been recommended by the 
EFC in its meeting held on 9/13.01.2025. The draft Cabinet Note has received the 
approval of Finance Minister on 19.02.2025.  The MSDE is in process of obtaining 
approval of Cabinet Note. Since the approval of the scheme is yet to be obtained, 
the funds could not be released in the FY.2024-25. It is expected that the scheme 
would receive approval in the current FY. Exact amount of release under the 
scheme will depend upon the time available in this FY after the Cabinet approval. 
The allocations in this scheme have been reduced to Rs. 294.00 Cr  at the RE 
stage. Meanwhile, pending the Cabinet approval, the Ministry has been permitted 
to spend only Rs. 10 Cr on the preparatory activities of the scheme.”  
 
96.  Budget allocation for the year 2024-25 was Rs.1000 crore, which was 
reduced to Rs. 294 crore at RE stage but no expenditure was incurred  as on 
15.01.2025 and BE for 2025-26 is Rs. 3000 crore although the BE proposed by 

 
61 
 
the Ministry was Rs. 5010 crore.  The allocated BE is thrice the BE for the FY 
2024-25. When asked about the reasons for the nil/zero expenditure during the 
current fiscal, how the RE of Rs. 294 crore is proposed to be utilized pending 
approval of the Cabinet for the Scheme and the factors taken into consideration 
for enhancement of BE in 2025-26, the Ministry stated as under:-      
“The New ITI Upgradation Scheme was announced in Union Budget 2024-
25. The initial BE of Rs. 1,000 crore was announced as part of the Budget 
announcement and was subsequently reduced to Rs. 294 crore anticipating the 
delay in the approval of the scheme by the Cabinet. The Committee would 
appreciate the fact that MSDE has undertaken wide stakeholder consultation 
involving industries, State/UT Governments and inter-ministerial consultation. 
The Expenditure Finance Committee in its meeting held on 09.01.2025 and 
13.01.2025 recommended the approval of the scheme. The MSDE is in the process 
of approval of Cabinet Note. Since the approval of the scheme has not been 
obtained, the funds could not be released in the FY 2024-25. It is expected that 
the scheme would be approved by the Cabinet before the end of the current 
financial year, and therefore, funds will be released for upgradation of ITIs. 
The RE for Rs. 294 crore has been proposed to be utilized for initiating 
implementation of the scheme once the approval is obtained. The enhancement of 
BE to Rs. 3,000 crore in 2025-26 has been made taking into consideration the 
requirement for full-scale implementation of the scheme.” 
 
97.   The Committee were apprised that the scheme is at the initial stage.  When  
asked about the steps taken to finalize the details of the new scheme and when it 
is proposed to be launched/rolled out, considering the fact that while Rs. 294 
crore is available during the current fiscal, Rs. 3000 crore has been allocated for 
2025-26. In reply, the Ministry submitted as under:-                
“The new scheme is being designed on the principles of Investment (need-
based and industry-relevant); Decentralization (aligned with industrial clusters 
and the local economy); Governance (industry-managed, outcome-based 
institutions, with accountability dovetailed with autonomy); and Trainer 
Development (scaling up NSTIs for trainer/professional development). MSDE has 
undertaken wide stakeholder consultation involving industries, State/UT 
governments, and inter-ministerial consultation, along with Workshops for 
Technical Knowledge Exchange with four countries (China, Germany, Singapore, 
and South Korea) to arrive at the design of the scheme. The scheme is proposed to 
be launched in March 2025.” 
 
98.    On being asked  about the status of the approval of the Scheme by the 
Cabinet and the preparedness/plan of action to utilize the funds earmarked for 
2024-25, the Ministry stated as follows:-     
“The approval of the Scheme by the Cabinet is currently in process. The 
Expenditure Finance Committee, in its meetings held on 09.01.2025 and 
13.01.2025, recommended the approval of the Scheme. The Ministry of Skill 
Development and Entrepreneurship is in the process of finalizing the Cabinet Note 
for approval. Since the Scheme has not yet been approved, the allocated funds 
could not be utilized in FY 2024-25. However, a Revised Estimate of Rs.294 crore 

 
62 
 
has been proposed to be utilized for initiating the implementation of the Scheme 
once approval is obtained.” 
99. The representative of the Ministry during evidence deposed as under:   
“The next xxx is with regard to the budgetary status of National Scheme of 
ITI's Upgradation. Budget estimates for 2024-25 was Rs.1,000 crores. In the 
revised estimates, we were given Rs.294 crore, but ultimately, pending Cabinet 
approval, DOI has permitted to spend only Rs.10 crores in the National Scheme of 
ITI upgradation for preparatory activities. The status of the scheme is that as of 
now the draft Cabinet note has been approved by the Finance Minister, and the 
Ministry is in the process of obtaining Cabinet approval.”  
100. The representative of the Ministry during evidence supplemented as under:   
“Secondly, the new scheme of ITI is quite an ambitious scheme. We are in 
the final stage of it. We have taken the approval of the Department of Expenditure 
as well as the approval of the Finance Minister. The new scheme which has been 
announced in this budget, which is about the five centres of excellence, efforts are 
being made to link them with this scheme. When we link both, our scheme will be 
approved. We have progressed a lot in that. Our guidelines are also being 
prepared. We have also talked to the state government and the industry so that we 
can give momentum to this scheme. We have structured this scheme keeping in 
mind our ITI system. We will try our best to improve the ITI infrastructure wise 
under the control of the state with the cooperation of the industry. We can de-
regulate them, give them freedom and strengthen their governance structure, we 
have edited this scheme keeping all these things in mind.”  
 
101.   The Scheme involves upgradation of 1000 ITIs in hub-and spoke 
arrangement i.e. 200 hubs and 800 spoke ITIs.  When asked about the criteria for 
selecting ITIs for upgradation, especially in terms of infrastructure, course 
contents, alignment with industry needs etc. the following information was 
furnished by the Ministry:-   
 
“The ITIs will be identified by State Governments in consultation with the 
industries and as per the guidelines issued by MSDE. It is informed that MSDE is 
in the process of preparing the scheme guidelines.” 
 
102.  The Committee were apprised that the key role of States/UTs will be 
identification of clusters.  It was also informed that the governance of the Scheme 
will be  Industry managed.  When asked to clarify as to how the Ministry will 
coordinate and monitor these aspects, the Ministry in their subsequent written 
reply stated as follows:-  (Post Evi.First Batch LoP 19)  
“The ITI falls under the administrative control of the State/UT government. 
Therefore, States/UTs serve as the primary drivers of the scheme, including the 
responsibility for cluster identification. Similarly, as announced in the Union 
Budget 2024 regarding the upgradation of 1,000 ITIs under a hub-and-spoke 
model with an outcome-oriented approach, the course content and design will be 

 
63 
 
aligned with industry skill needs. Consequently, an industry-led governance 
structure has been proposed.  
Regarding the role of the Central Government, the scheme will be 
monitored by the National Steering Committee, headed by the Secretary, MSDE. 
This committee will play a key role in finalizing operational guidelines, monitoring 
progress, and recommending necessary course corrections. Furthermore, the final 
approval of the Strategic Investment Plan, as recommended by the States, will be 
granted by the Centre. The Central Government will also monitor Key Performance 
Indicators (KPIs) through third-party evaluations and conduct regular meetings to 
track implementation progress.”                                             
103. When asked as to what extent the new Scheme is expected to supplement 
the infrastructure deficiencies in the skilling of manpower in the country and 
cater to the needs of emerging sectors like electronics, renewable energy and 
automation to meet the skills demand in both the national and global job 
markets, the Ministry responded as under:-  
 
“The scheme proposes a hub and spoke model for upgradation of ITIs. A 
hub ITI will have, on an average, four (4) spoke ITIs. Upgraded ITIs are envisioned 
to be equipped with state-of-the-art infrastructure, machinery, and equipment, 
with proper space and facility planning for procurement and placement of required 
lab resources as per the course and curriculum plan. It will ensure that the 
students receive high-quality learning through modern facilities and up-to-date 
equipment, all of which making the ITIs aspirational. On an average, four (4) new 
courses would be introduced, and ten (10) existing courses would be upgraded at 
the hub ITIs. On an average, two (2) new courses would be introduced, and eight 
(8) existing courses would be upgraded in spoke ITIs. The newly introduced trades 
will cater to the emerging sectors like electronics, renewable energy and 
automation to meet the skills demand in both the national and global job 
markets.” 
 
104.  On being asked to provide details of the proposed mechanism to monitor 
and assess the likely impact of the proposed New ITIs Upgradation Scheme on the 
skilling and employment outcomes of the youth in the country, the Ministry 
submitted as under:-  
“Yes, there will be a detailed monitoring framework for the scheme, which 
will be tracked. The scheme will focus on results in two complementary ways. 
First, it will provide a monitoring framework that will include ambitious targets 
and cover inputs, outputs, outcomes, timelines, measurement parameters, 
mechanisms for measurement, and validation. It will focus strengthening 
governance, industry linkages, infrastructure, and training to ensure alignment 
with evolving industry needs.    
To ensure accountability, each hub-and-spoke cluster will be required to 
submit a comprehensive Strategic Investment Plan (SIP) upfront, adhering to the 
provided template. These plans will include measurable parameters for inputs, 
outputs, and outcomes, along with timelines. Progress will be closely monitored, 
through regular reporting and reviewed against these predefined metrics.  
Second, the funding under the scheme will be provided on a performance 
basis, i.e., when certain key performance indicators are achieved. These key 

 
64 
 
performance indicators will be Disbursement Linked Indicators (DLIs) specified in 
results-based loans from the World Bank and ADB and will cascade down from 
the Centre to States to ITIs. 
Moreover, the World Bank and ADB will bring expertise in supporting the 
Ministry to carry out an impact evaluation of the scheme. The combination of this 
impact evaluation and the independent verification of the achievement of DLIs will 
provide robust evidence of the success of the scheme. 
To support implementation and tracking, a five-year investment plan and a 
set of performance indicators for measuring success will be included as part of 
scheme guidelines.”

F.  THE PROJECT 'SWAVALAMBINI' 
106. The Project 'Swavalambini Women Entrepreneurship Programme' is 
specifically targeted at female students of colleges and universities. The National 
Institute for Entrepreneurship and Small Business Development (NIESBUD), 
Noida and the Indian Institute of Entrepreneurship (IIE), Guwahati, will be the 
Implementing Agency (IA) of the Project 'Swavalambini' of MSDE in collaboration 
with NITI Aayog.   
 
107. The initiative will focus on empowering female students in Higher 
Education Institutions (HEIS) by providing them with essential skills, mentorship, 
and access to resources necessary for starting and scaling successful businesses. 
The Project will focus on comprehensive entrepreneurship training/ capacity-
building combining theory-based training with practical exposure through 
experiential learning.   

 
72 
 
 
108. The project will be implemented  in Banaras Hindu University, Chaudhary 
Charan Singh University,  University of Hyderabad, Maulana Azad National Urdu 
University, Kiang Nangba Government College, Jowai, Ri- Bhoi College, Ri Bhoi 
and North Eastern Hill University (NEHU), Shillong,  Government Champai 
College, Lunglei Government College and Mizoram University and  Gauhati 
University, Handique College and Dispur College.  
 
109. The target of the project is 1200 female students under Entrepreneurship 
Awareness Programme (NIESBUD - 600, IIE - 600), out of which, 600 will be 
further selected for the Women Entrepreneurship Development Programme 
(NIESBUD-300, IIE - 300). The programme will be implemented in four phases. 
 
110. When asked to provide details of the Project inter-alia indicating the 
implementation period, criteria for selection of Universities and students, 
preparedness of Implementing Agencies, budgetary allocation, tentative intake in 
each University/College, plan of action for implementation of four phases of the 
Project, etc., the Ministry responded as under:-     
 
“A brief Note on the Implementation of the Swavalambini Women 
Entrepreneurship Programme is as under: 
 
The Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE) in 
collaboration with NITI Aayog and Women Entrepreneurship Platform (WEP) as 
knowledge partner, has launched the Swavalambini Women Entrepreneurship 
Programme on 07th February 2025 in North Eastern states of India as Meghalaya, 
Mizoram and Assam.  
The Swavalambini Project is designed to foster an entrepreneurial mindset 
among women students, making them aware of the available support 
mechanisms, schemes, resources, and networks necessary to pursue 
entrepreneurship as a career. The project will also be launched as a pilot in 
selected colleges and universities of Uttar Pradesh and Telangana. The National 
Institute of Entrepreneurship and Small Business Development (NIESBUD) and 
Indian Institute of Entrepreneurship (IIE) shall be the implementing partners for 
the pilot project. 
1. Implementation Period 
The Swavalambini Women Entrepreneurship Programme will be 
implemented in selected colleges and HEIs, ensuring adequate time for planning, 
execution, and monitoring across all phases. The programme will include Faculty 
Development Programmes (FDP) of 5 days for selected faculty members from 
colleges, Entrepreneurship Awareness Programmes (EAP) of 2 days for 1,200 
students, Entrepreneurship Development Programmes (EDP) of 40 hours for 
selected 600 students, followed by 6 months of mentoring and handholding 
support to ensure sustained guidance and business development assistance. 
2. Criteria for Selection of Universities and Students 
 Universities & Colleges Selection Criteria: 

 
73 
 
The selection of institutions for this initiative will prioritize those with a 
well-established ecosystem for entrepreneurship and innovation, ensuring a 
strong foundation for fostering startups and business ventures. Additionally, the 
availability of dedicated faculty and institutional support for entrepreneurship 
programs will be considered in the selection process. Furthermore, institutions 
with the potential for scaling the initiative within their academic framework will be 
preferred, allowing for long-term sustainability and broader impact. 
 Student Selection Criteria: 
A customized online application form will be created and hosted on Skill 
India Digital Hub (SIDH) portal and the WEP platform for initial selection of the 
1200 students from the selected colleges.All the selected candidates shall also be 
registered on the NIESBUD portal/IIE portal and on SIDH which will track the 
complete life cycle of the trainee and provide inputs on its progress.  
Selected Institutions participating in the will also disseminate the 
application form through their internal communication channels.Faculties trained 
through Faculty Development Programme shall support in mobilizing the students 
for the programme. 
The selection mechanism for the Entrepreneurship Awareness Programme 
(EAP) and the Women Entrepreneurship Development Programme (WEDP) will 
follow a structured and merit-based approach.  
 Initially, collaboration with participating institutions will be undertaken to 
identify and finalize the top 1,200 applicants (150 from each institution) for 
the EAP.  
 To assess entrepreneurial interest and potential, a well-designed Aptitude 
Test will be developed and administered to all EAP participants.  
 Based on the test results, the top 600 candidates will be selected for the 
WEDP. 
 Additionally, a Selection Committee will be constituted to oversee the 
shortlisting process, ensuring transparency and fairness. Regular meetings 
will be organized to review applications and finalize the list of selected 
candidates. 
3. Preparedness of Implementing Agencies (IAs) 
 The Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE) has been 
working for promoting entrepreneurship development amongst women, 
marginalized communities, and individuals from lower socio-economic 
backgrounds in the country through its autonomous Institutes, namely, 
National Institute for Entrepreneurship and Small Business Development 
(NIESBUD), Noida and Indian Institute of Entrepreneurship (IIE), Guwahati.  
 Both the institutes deliver Entrepreneurship Awareness Programmes (EAP), 
Entrepreneurship Development Programmess (EDP), Faculty Development 
Programmes (FDP), Entrepreneurship and Skill Development Programmes 
(ESDP) along with Mentoring and handholding support to aspiring and 
existing entrepreneurs across the country through their centres and in 
partnership with various other stakeholders. 
 Over the past ten years, both NIESBUD and IIE have collectively trained 
12,33,699 candidates through various programs and interventions, 

 
74 
 
demonstrating their significant contribution to the entrepreneurial 
ecosystem. Notably, 7,06,617 (57.27%) of these trainees have been women, 
highlighting their commitment to promoting women’s entrepreneurship and 
inclusive economic growth. 
4. Budgetary Allocation 
 The estimated budget for the program includes funding for faculty training, 
student training, mentorship support, outreach, and operational costs. 
 Financial provisions for seed funding and awards for high-potential 
startups will be facilitated with the support of NITI Aayog under the Award 
to Reward (ATR) Initiative. 
 Budgetary details will be finalized based on institutional agreements and 
approvals. 
5. Tentative Intake in Each University/College 
The target intake is 1,200 female students under the Entrepreneurship 
Awareness Programme (EAP), with a further selection of 600 students for the 
Women Entrepreneurship Development Programme (WEDP).  
The specific intake for each university/college will be determined based on 
institutional capacity and interest levels. 
6. Plan of Action for Implementation of the Four Phases 
 Phase I: Faculty Development Program (FDP) (5 Days) 
o Train selected faculty members from participating institutions. 
o Ensure trained faculty are equipped to guide students effectively. 
 Phase II: Entrepreneurship Awareness Programme (EAP) (2 Days) 
o Mobilize students with the support of trained faculty. 
o Conduct awareness sessions for 1,200 students. 
 Phase III: Women Entrepreneurship Development Programme (WEDP) 
(40 Hours) 
o Selection and Identification of 600 students for advanced entrepreneurship 
training. 
o Training to focus on six key areas as entrepreneurial skills, access to 
finance, market linkages, compliance and legal requirements, mentoring 
and networking, and business development services to prepare these 
students for a career as an entrepreneur. 
 Phase IV: Mentoring and Handholding Support (21 Weeks: 2-3 Hours 
Per Week) 
o Provide personalized mentorship and industry exposure for the trained 
students. 
o Facilitate access to funding, incubation, and market opportunities with the 
support of NITI Aayog and WEP. 

 
75 
 
o Recognize and showcase successful women entrepreneurs.”

114.  The Committee note that the Skill Acquisition and Knowledge Awareness 
for Livelihood Promotion (SANKALP) was launched in January 2018, with an 
implementation period until March 2023, which has been extended till March 
2025. When enquired whether the Scheme which has been able to achieve its 
objectives and whether there is any proposal to extend the Scheme beyond 
March, 2025 or introduce any other Scheme on similar lines, the Ministry 
submitted as under:- 
“SANKALP included four Project Development Objectives (PDOs). The 
targets set for all  the four PDOs under the project have been achieved.  
 PDO Indicator 1: At least 42,00,000 Trainees who have successfully completed 
the market-relevant short-term SD programs and were certified (disaggregated by 
women and disadvantaged sections). 
Target Achievement: 50,41,262 trainees successfully completed the market-
relevant short-term SD programs and were certified. 
 PDO Indicator 2: At least 40% of graduates who are wage employed or self-
employed within six months of completion of short-term SD programs.   
Target Achievement: 40.33% graduates placed/self-employed within six months 
of completion of SD program training. 
 PDO Indicator 3: At least six Participating States have improved their SIG scores 
by 10% of the performance gap over the previous year, Improved performance of 
states on institutional strengthening, market relevance of SD programs, and 
access to and completion of training by marginalized populations.  
Target Achievement: i) SIG Manual has been developed by MSDE; ii) Baseline for 
SIG scorecard has been developed for all participating state; iii) 21 participating 
states have improved their SIG scores by 15% of the performance gap. 
 PDO Indicator 4: NSQF aligned QPs translated into teaching learning materials

Further, the targets for all the Disbursement Linked Indicators (DLIs) have been

Verification Agency and expected to be completed by March 2025.

119.  With regard to Training Courses and Standards, the Committee were 
apprised that 4500 qualifications have been approved. However, the Ministry has

the status of the remaining 1411 qualifications, the Ministry stated as under:-  
“The National Skill Qualification Framework (NSQF) alignment and 
approval of qualifications is a dynamic process wherein the qualifications are 
approved periodically in accordance with the industry requirements for imparting 
need-based skill trainings. The NSQF aligned and approved qualifications are 

 
81 
 
reflected in the National Qualification Register (NQR) portal, which is a centralized 
repository for all such qualifications.  
To maintain the relevance and currency of these qualifications, the 
qualifications are approved with a validity period of 3 years, unless otherwise 
specified by the NSQC. Upon completion of this period, the qualifications are 
revised by incorporating necessary technological and other changes.  
Additionally, to ensure that only relevant and industry driven qualifications 
remain active in the skilling ecosystem, NCVET follows the prescribed process of 
periodical archival of qualifications which fall under the below mentioned criteria: 
a) The validity of the qualification has expired and the awarding bodies 
concerned have not taken up the same for revision, hence all such qualifications 
are deemed to be not required in the skill ecosystem. 
b) Any entity which had got the qualifications NSQF aligned either during the 
time of NSDA or till 2021 with NCVET and is presently not a recognized awarding 
body (AB) of NCVET. 
c) All such Qualifications where there is no training conducted and/or are 
inactive for more than a year. 
d) Qualifications which have not been rationalized as per the National Credit 
Framework (NCrF) and revised National Skills Qualification Framework (NSQF).  
e) The NCVET recognized awarding body has requested deactivation/archiving 
of their qualifications.  
Accordingly, the NSQC in its meetings, based on the criteria above, 
undertakes regular archival of qualifications. Based on this, as on date (till 41st 
NSQC), a total of 8151 qualifications have been NSQF aligned and approved of 
which 5062 qualifications have been archived so far. Presently, 3089 NSQF 
aligned and approved qualifications are valid and active.”

Jan Shikshan Sansthan (JSS):-The Jan Shikshan Sansthan (JSS) Scheme, 
initially launched as Shramik Vidyapeeth (SVP) in 1967, aims to provide skill 
training in a non-formal mode at the doorsteps of the beneficiary through 
registered Societies (NGOs) with 100% grant from the Government of India. The 
objective of the scheme is to increase the household income by promoting 
self/wage employment through skill development training. The target 
beneficiaries of the scheme are non-literates, neo-literates and persons having 
rudimentary level of education, school dropouts up to class 12th in the age group 
of 15-45 years. The priority groups are women, SCs, STs, OBCs and minorities in 
the rural areas and urban low-income areas.

122.   It has been noticed that there were 15,012 ITIs in 2023-24 viz-a-viz 14,619 
in 2024-25 i.e. there is reduction of 393 ITIs. Similarly, there is reduction in the 
number of seats from 26 lakhs in 2023-24 to 23.17 lakhs in 2024-25. When the 
Committee asked the reasons for reduction in the number of ITIs as well as the 
number of seats, the Ministry in their subsequent written reply stated as under:-               
                                                     
“The Directorate General of Training has introduced an objective 
methodology for grading of Industrial Training Institutes (ITIs) from 2023.  This 
Data Driven Grading Methodology (DDGM) is based on several parameters 
available in the DGT-MIS portal, on the basis of which ITIs are awarded 
numerical grading.  
While implementing this methodology, discrepancies have been found in 
the data, especially regarding the number of seats in ITIs which were found to be 
lying vacant for several years. This was affecting the grading of an ITI, as 
‘admission percentage’ which is an important criterion in the DDGM gets 
wrongly reflected. Further, sanitization and accuracy of data is also essential for 
preparation of the correct seat matrix for admission and furnishing of 
information to various important forums. 
As per DGT letter no. DGT-12/01/2018-TC (Part) dated 20.12.2018, any 
trade or unit with zero admissions for two consecutive years will be deactivated. 
DGT granted a one-time relaxation in 2022 for ITIs with 100% vacant seats for 
two consecutive years due to the Covid-19 pandemic. 
To optimize seating capacity, DGT conducted a review to identify seats 
continuously vacant for five years. After considering representations from ITIs

apprised that the fund release under the Scheme has been restored post 
Cabinet approval for Skill India Programme on 07.02.2025 and all pending 
DBT payment will be taken care. In addition, steps for payment of stipend of 
Rs.200 crore  are being taken and, accordingly, the estimated expenditure 
will reach Rs. 582 crore by 31.03.2025. The Committee appreciate that 
despite approval of the Scheme being accorded in February, 2025, the 
Ministry will be able to incur expenditure  almost equal to enhanced RE of 
Rs. 600 crore in 2024-25.  The Committee desire that the momentum  be 
continued unabated so as to fully utilize Rs. 600 crore allocated during 
2025-26 also. 
 22. The Committee, however, find that against the physical target of 12 
lakh intended apprentices during 2024-25, as on 28.02.2025, 9 lakh 
apprentices have been engaged and 3 lakh beneficiaries are yet to be 
engaged. According to the Ministry, around one lakh apprentices are getting 
added every month. Consequently, there will still be shortfall of 2 lakh 
beneficiaries, as such, the Ministry may not be able to achieve the physical 
target set for 2024-25.  The Committee desire that the efforts be made to 
cover the remaining 20.62 lakh beneficiaries by 2025-26, being the 
culmination year of the Scheme.  
 
23.  The Committee note that as on 31st January, 2025, 21259 
establishments have engaged 8,22,196 apprentices and out of them, 6,643 
(0.81%) have been engaged by 408 establishments located in North-Eastern 
Region (NER) States. The Committee, thus find that the NER offers 
significantly lesser apprenticeship opportunities compared to the rest of the 
country. Therefore, considering the inherent issues of the States of the 
North Eastern Region, the Ministry is contemplating a Pilot project 
exclusively for NER to promote apprenticeship for which a Concept Note is 
in the draft stage. The Committee feel that implementation of the NAPS is 
marred with shortfall in North Eastern Region. The Committee would, 

 
112 
 
therefore, like to impress upon the Ministry to take up the Concept Note for 
pilot project on NER on priority basis so to undertake capacity building of 
the apprenticeship ecosystem for the people of the NER.  
24. The Committee note that while there is persistent increase in BE for 
NER during the last three years i.e. from Rs. 291.32 crore in 2022-23 to Rs. 
332.15 crore in 2023-24 to Rs. 431.31 crore (as on 15.01.2025) in 2024-25, 
the actual expenditure of the Ministry for the region has decreased during 
the corresponding period viz. from 22.83% to 22.42% to 18.26% 
respectively, i.e., more than 75% funds were not utilised every year.  The 
Committee further note that during 2024-25, as on 18.02.2025, of the total 
allocation of Rs. 431.31 crore (9.54% of Ministry’s BE) the Ministry’s NER 
expenditure is Rs. 144.12 crore and, as stated by the Ministry, it is 
estimated to reach Rs.170 crore by the end of the current fiscal, which is 
significantly higher than previous year (Rs. 74.50 crore in 2023-24 and Rs. 
66.52 crore in 2022-23). The Committee, however, find that Rs. 261.31 
crore shall still remain unutilized by 31.03.2025. Considering the fact that 
Skill India Programme has now been approved by the Cabinet, the 
Committee expect that allocation of Rs. 509.85 crore for NER will be fully 
utilized during 2025-26.  
25. The Committee, while appreciating that to promote apprenticeship, 
the Ministry have organized Pradhan Mantri National Apprenticeship Melas 
(PMNAMs) at 190 locations/districts, since 2022-23 in the North Eastern 
Region (NER), wish to point out that not even a single establishment 
participated in the PMNAM organised in Meghalaya, Mizoram and Nagaland 
and desire that while organising PMNAMs particularly in NER, it needs to be 
ensured that the registered establishments do participate in such Melas.   
 
 26. The Committee note that during 2024-25, out of 9,00,616 apprentices 
engaged as on 28.02.2025, 6,95,808 are men and 2,04,808 are women.  As 
stated by the Ministry, the difference in apprentice engagement when 
compared to FY 2023-24 has exceeded by 7,910 (4% increase than FY 2023-

 
113 
 
24) in case of women apprentices and in case of men, it is 39,596 (5.4% 
lesser than FY 2023-24). The Committee have been apprised that it is 
expected that achievement during the current FY will not be less when 
compared to FY 2023-24. The Committee have also been apprised that to 
increase women participation in apprentices, the Ministry propose to 
organize PMNAM  with a focus on mobilization from women centric 
Institutions (Women’s College and Vocational Training Centres) as well as 
development and promotion of  apprenticeship  in   Sectors with high 
growth potential and traditionally higher female participation such as 
healthcare, IT/ITES, and retail.  Observing that apprentice engagement is 
dynamic and keeps on progressing throughout the year,  the Committee 
desire that in addition to the measures being taken by the Ministry, the 
other innovative measures also need to be taken so as to increase women 
participation in apprentices so that women have access to relevant and in-
demand skills. 
27.  The Committee note that out of 25.38 lakh apprentices engaged  w.e.f. 
2022-23 upto 18.02.2025, 11.37 lakh candidates (44%) belonged to SC, ST 
and OBC [2.97 lakh SCs, 1.12 lakh STs, and 7.28 lakh OBCs].  The 
Committee have been apprised that although there is no target allocation 
based on social category, the Ministry vide letter dated 28.01.2025 have 
requested all State Commissioners/Directors dealing with Skilling/ 
Apprenticeship Training and State Skill Development Missions to further 
sensitize the identified vulnerable pockets about all  PMNAM events. The 
Committee while appreciating the steps taken by the Ministry emphasise 
that periodic review of such measures be undertaken so as to ensure that 
social category candidates are not deprived of the benefits of the Scheme. 
   
28. The Committee note that there is persistent increase in candidates 
dropped out during the last three years. During 2022-23, 2023-24, and 
2024-25, 2.34 lakh, 2.37 lakh and 2.89 lakh candidates respectively had 
dropped out from their apprentices training. The reasons for such drop out 

 
114 
 
inter-alia included  relocation challenges from place of living to 
establishment location at new location; factory/industry/establishment 
environment; cost of living; environmental conditions; health, etc.  In 
addition, attractive alternative options also lead to dropout in 
apprenticeship training.  The Committee have been apprised that the 
Ministry have taken measures like organisation of Workshops/awareness 
programmes to sensitize various stakeholders and Pradhan Mantri National 
Apprenticeship Mela (PMNAM) to facilitate as a platform to disseminate 
information on apprenticeship training.  The Ministry have also informed 
that besides revision of minimum stipend rates, efforts will also be made for 
a supportive workplace culture by establishments and States/ UTs will also 
be sensitized to make use of PMNAM/ workshops/ awareness programme to 
disseminate information for assisting interested persons to take informed 
decisions before joining the apprenticeship training. Observing that increase 
in drop out of apprentices is a matter of serious concern, the Committee 
recommend that the challenges faced by apprentices need to be addressed 
with utmost sincerity and desire that the action proposed to be taken by 
the Ministry needs to be taken to logical conclusion so as to minimize 
dropout of apprentices. 
V. NATIONAL SCHEME FOR ITIs UPGRADATION  
 
29.    Announced in budget 2024-25, the National Scheme for Upgradation of 
ITIs aims to enhance the quality and outcomes of skilling across India by 
upgrading 1,000 ITIs in a hub-and-spoke arrangement over five years. The 
BE for 2024-25 is Rs. 3000.00 crore, which has been reduced to Rs.294 
crore as the Scheme is yet to be approved by the Cabinet. For 2025-26, 
against the demand of  Rs.5010 crore, the Ministry of Finance agreed for an 
allocation of Rs.3000.00 crore. 
 
The Committee have been apprised that the Scheme has been 
recommended by the EFC in its meetings held on 09.01.2025 and 
13.01.2025, the draft Cabinet Note has received the approval of Finance 

 
115 
 
Minister on 19.02.2025 and the MSDE is in the process of obtaining 
approval of Cabinet Note. The Committee have also been apprised that since 
the approval of the Scheme is yet to be obtained, the funds could not be 
released in the FY 2024-25. The Ministry have also stated that it is expected 
that the Scheme would receive approval in the current FY and the exact 
amount of release under the scheme will depend upon the time available in 
this FY after the Cabinet approval. Meanwhile, pending the Cabinet 
approval, the Ministry have been permitted to spend only Rs. 10 crore on 
the preparatory activities of the scheme. 
  
The Committee have also been apprised that a wide range of 
stakeholder consultation involving industries, State/UT governments, and 
inter-ministerial consultation has been undertaken. In addition, Workshops 
for Technical Knowledge Exchange with four countries (China, Germany, 
Singapore, and South Korea) to arrive at the design of the scheme have also 
been conducted. The Scheme is proposed to be launched in March 2025.  
 
The Committee further note that the ITIs will be identified by State 
Governments in consultation with the industries, as per the guidelines 
issued by MSDE and the Ministry is in the process of preparing the scheme 
guidelines. The Committee have been apprised that building on the 
initiative announced in previous budget, five National Centres of Excellence 
for skilling will be set up with global expertise and partnerships to equip our 
youth with the skills required for “Make for India, Make for the World” 
manufacturing. A suitable mechanism for setting up of five National Centres 
of Excellence for skilling is under process in the Ministry, and, as informed 
by the representative of the Ministry during evidence, the Ministry propose 
to align the Scheme with National Scheme for ITI upgradation. 
 The Committee, while appreciating the efforts being made to prepare 
detailed guidelines, aligning the Scheme with the Scheme of setting up of 
five National Centres of Excellence for skilling as announced in Budget 
2025-26 and pursuing for necessary approval of the Scheme, expect that the 

 
116 
 
necessary approval will be accorded soon and the Ministry will be able to 
utilise the reduced RE during March 2025 and also budget estimates of Rs. 
3000 crore in 2025-26. 
VI. SCHEMES FOR PROMOTION OF ENTREPRENEURHIP 
 
 (i)  Pradhan Mantri Janjati Adivasi Nyaya Maha Abhiyan (PM-JANMAN):  
 
30. The Committee note that the Ministry of Skill Development and 
Entrepreneurship (MSDE), through its autonomous institutes, Indian 
Institute of Entrepreneurship (IIE) and National Institute of 
Entrepreneurship and Small Business Development (NIESBUD) is 
undertaking the skill development training component of PM JANMAN 
Scheme of the Ministry of Tribal Affairs (MoTA) with the support of the 
Tribal Cooperative Marketing Development Federation of India (TRIFED). It 
is aimed at targeted development of 75 Particularly Vulnerable Tribal 
Groups (PVTGs) residing in 15 States.  
 
Under this project, a total of 500 Van Dhan Vikas Kendras (VDVKs) are 
to be set up by TRIFED and a total of 42,000 PVTG beneficiaries are to be 
trained during 2024-25 & 2025-26. As on 19.02.2025, 174 VDVKs have been 
established and 326 VDVKs are yet to be set up. The responsibility of 
NIESBUD and IIE is to implement the skilling component of the Project 
while setting up of VDVKs lies with TRIFED. From the target of 42,000 
PVTG beneficiaries to be trained, 39,576 beneficiaries have been covered 
through Entrepreneurship Awareness Programmes (EAP). Out of the total 
trained under EAP, 31,547 beneficiaries have been trained through 
Entrepreneurship Development Programmes (EDP) of which 20,492 
beneficiaries, have been further trained through Value Added Skill Training 
(VAT). The training programmes are ongoing and the Ministry have assured 
that the rest of the beneficiaries are expected to be trained before 31st 
March, 2025. The Committee expect the Ministry to make concerted efforts 
and honour their commitment to cover beneficiaries who are yet to be 

 
117 
 
trained. The Committee also desire that the remaining 326 VDVKs be set up 
by TRIFED in the larger interest of the intended beneficiaries. 
 
(ii)  PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana Entrepreneurship Skill Development 
Programme 
 
31. The Committee note that the Ministry in collaboration with the 
Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE) are organizing 
Entrepreneurship Development Programme (EDP) on Solar Entrepreneurship 
under the PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana. The Ministry are implementing 
the programme through their autonomous institute, NIESBUD which has 
received the sanction from the MNRE in the month of September, 2024 for 
implementing the programme during F.Y. 2024 - 25 and F.Y. 2025 – 26 with 
a total target of 50,000. 
The Committee further note that as on 28th February, 2025, the 
Institute has imparted training to 6,900 participants under the project viz., 
only14% beneficiaries have been covered and the remaining 86% are to be 
covered by 31.03.2026. The Committee impress upon the Ministry to 
intensify the efforts and cover the remaining beneficiaries by the target 
date.  
32. The Committee have been apprised that the target group to be covered 
under the programme are either the existing vendors or the new 
entrepreneurs who have the capacity to become empanelled vendors by 
submitting bank guarantee of Rs. 2.50 Lakh as per the guidelines framed by 
the MNRE. In the considered opinion of the Committee, the bank guarantee 
of Rs. 2.50 Lakh may stand a stumbling block for many especially the 
vendors in the rural areas. The Committee, therefore, desire the Ministry to 
take up the matter regarding review of the guidelines with the Ministry of 
New and Renewable Energy so as to reduce the amount of Bank guarantee.  
 
(iii)  Raising & Accelerating MSME Performance (RAMP)  

 
118 
 
33. The Committee note that the Ministry through their autonomous 
Institute viz. NIESBUD are organising  Sensitization and Capacity Building 
Workshop for Women Entrepreneurs sponsored by Maharashtra Small Scale 
Industries Development Corporation Limited (MSSIDC) under Raising and 
Accelerating MSME Performance (RAMP) scheme of the Ministry of Micro, 
Small and Medium Enterprises (MoMSME). The Committee further note that 
the Capacity Building workshops organised by NIESBUD under the initiative 
aims to support 10,000 women-led MSMEs across Maharashtra by providing 
them with essential knowledge on key aspects such as entrepreneurial 
ecosystems, regulatory compliance, government schemes, digital marketing, 
e-commerce, financial literacy, and legal compliance for scaling their 
businesses.  
The Committee have been apprised that the project has been 
sanctioned to NIESBUD in the month of September 2024 for implementing 
the programme in F.Y. - 2024-25 and F.Y. 2025-26. During the first phase, 
NIESBUD has to impart training to 3,000 participants by 31 March, 2025 
and as on 28th  February, 2025, the Institute has imparted training to 2,207 
participants. The Committee have also been apprised that the Institute has 
mobilised the participants for the remaining target and is organising the 
programmes in different districts of Maharashtra, as such, the allocated 
target will be completed by 31st March 2025. The Ministry have also stated 
that in the second phase, the Institute is required to train 7,000 
participants by 31st March 2026. 
The Committee find that while 30% target will be achieved by 
31.03.2025, the remaining 70% beneficiaries will be required to be covered 
in 2025-26. The Committee, therefore, call upon the Ministry to draw a road 
map for achieving the target within the stipulated time.   
(iv) Capacity Building for Fair Price Shop Owners (FPS) 
34. The Committee note that the Ministry in collaboration with the 
Department of Food and Public Distribution (DFPD), Ministry of Consumer 

 
119 
 
Affairs, Food and Public Distribution have undertaken a Capacity Building 
Programme for Fair Price Shop (FPS) Owners. The project is aimed to enable 
the FPS owners to run their businesses in consonance with the 
contemporary practices being adopted by Retail Entrepreneurs. The 
Committee have been apprised that the Ministry, through their autonomous 
Institute viz. NIESBUD is responsible for training and capacity building, 
while the nomination of participants is provided by DFPD in consultation 
with the respective State Food Distribution Departments. The total target 
under the project is to train 3000 FPS owners by 31st March, 2026 and, out 
of them, the number of beneficiaries trained till 20th February, 2025 is 318 
and further training of 300 more beneficiaries is planned to be completed by 
31.03.2025. 
The Committee, thus, find that while 20% target will be achieved by 
31.03.2025, the remaining 80% beneficiaries will be required to be covered 
in 2025-26. The Committee call upon the Ministry to coordinate with DFPD 
and achieve the target as stipulated above. 
VII. PROJECT 'SWAVALAMBINI WOMEN ENTREPRENEURSHIP 
PROGRAMME' 
 
35. The Committee note that the Project 'Swavalambini Women 
Entrepreneurship Programme' is specifically targeted at female students of 
colleges and universities. NIESBUD, Noida and the IIE, Guwahati, will be the 
Implementing Agency (IA) of the Project 'Swavalambini' of MSDE in 
collaboration with NITI Aayog.   The initiative will focus on empowering 
female students in Higher Education Institutions (HEIS) by providing them 
with essential skills, mentorship, and access to resources necessary for 
starting and scaling successful businesses. The Project will focus on 
comprehensive entrepreneurship training/ capacity-building combining 
theory-based training with practical exposure through experiential learning.   
 
The Committee further note that the Project will be implemented  in 
Banaras Hindu University and Chaudhary Charan Singh University (North 

 
120 
 
Zone-Uttar Pradesh);  University of Hyderabad, Maulana Azad National Urdu 
University, (South Zone-Telangana);  Kiang Nangba Government College, 
Jowai, Ri- Bhoi College, Ri Bhoi and North Eastern Hill University (NEHU), 
Shillong (North East Zone-Meghalaya);  Government Champai College, 
Lunglei Government College and Mizoram University (North East Zone-
Mizoram); and Gauhati University, Handique College and Dispur College 
(North East Zone-Assam). The target of the Project is to train 1200 female 
students under Entrepreneurship Awareness Programme (NIESBUD - 600, IIE 
- 600), out of which, 600 will be further selected for the Women 
Entrepreneurship Development Programme (NIESBUD-300, IIE - 300).  
 
The Committee were apprised that the Ministry of Skill Development 
and Entrepreneurship (MSDE) in collaboration with NITI Aayog and Women 
Entrepreneurship Platform (WEP) as knowledge partner, have recently 
launched the Swavalambini Women Entrepreneurship Programme on 07th 
February, 2025 in North Eastern States of India viz. Meghalaya, Mizoram 
and Assam.  The Committee impress upon the Ministry to take necessary 
steps to ensure that the Project is launched/implemented in the already 
selected Higher Education Institutions (HEIS) of the remaining two States 
viz. Uttar Pradesh and Telengana. 
 
36. The Committee have been apprised that the programme will be 
implemented in four phases and will include Faculty Development 
Programmes (FDP) of 5 days for selected faculty members from colleges, 
Entrepreneurship Awareness Programmes (EAP) of 2 days for 1,200 students, 
Entrepreneurship Development Programmes (EDP) of 40 hours for selected 
600 students, followed by 6 months of mentoring and handholding support 
to ensure sustained guidance and business development assistance. The 
Committee desire that it would be in the fitness of things if  the feedback is 
also obtained from trained faculty and students selected as well as trained 
after every phase of the Project so as to have an objective assessment of 
shortcomings as well as improvement in future training programmes. 
 

 
121 
 
37. The Committee have also been apprised that over the past ten years, 
both NIESBUD and IIE have collectively trained 12,33,699 candidates 
through various programs and interventions, demonstrating their 
significant contribution to the entrepreneurial ecosystem and notably, 
7,06,617 (57.27%) of these trainees have been women. The Committee 
appreciate the contribution made by both NIESBUD and IIE and their 
commitment to promoting women’s entrepreneurship and inclusive 
economic growth and desire both organizations  to maintain momentum so 
as to ensure attainment of the  objectives of the  Project. 
VIII  PM-VISHWAKARMA  
38. The Committee note that PM Vishwakarma Scheme was launched on 
17th September, 2023, which aims at upskilling the Vishwakarma’s with the 
knowledge of modern tools and techniques coupled with credit support for 
expanding their business. The Scheme is being implemented by three 
Ministries i.e., Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSME), 
Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE), and 
Department of Financial Services (DFS), Ministry of Finance and MSDE is 
the nodal ministry for implementation of Skilling Component of the 
Scheme. A total of 18 trades are covered under the Scheme to promote 
onboarding of training centres under the scheme.  
    The Committee note that as on 15.02.2025, PMV id is available in 679 
districts, however, training has been initiated in 636 districts, the training 
is yet to be initiated in 43 districts. Further, 26,96,358 PMV ID are available 
and as on 15.02.2025, 18,99,385 candidates have been trained and assessed 
against the target of 16 lakh candidates for 2023-24 and 2024-25.  
The Committee observe that the PM Vishwakarma Yojana is currently 
available in 34 out of 36 States/ Union Territories except Tamil Nadu and 
West Bengal. The Ministry have stated that the State Monitoring Committee 
and District Implementation Committees have not yet been constituted by 
these two States. The Committee recommend the Ministry to take up the 

 
122 
 
matter with the two State Governments without any further delay and 
resolve the issue so that products and services of artisans of the two States 
also have their benevolent share in domestic and global value chains. The 
Committee would like to be apprised of the progress made in this regard. 
39. The Ministry have further stated that the concerned State 
Governments and Regional Directorates of Skill Development and 
Entrepreneurship will work together to identify suitable training centers to 
initiate training in the remaining 43 districts. The Committee desire the 
Ministry to strengthen their coordination and monitoring mechanism so as 
to ensure identification and operationalisation of Training Centres in 43 
disticts on urgent basis so that the deserving artisans peddle their products 
and services into domestic and global value chains.  
IX. SKILL ACQUISITION AND KNOWLEDGE AWARENESS FOR LIVELIHOOD 
PROMOTION (SANKALP) 
40. The Committee note that the Skill Acquisition and Knowledge 
Awareness for Livelihood Promotion (SANKALP) was conceived to support 
National Skill Development Mission (NSDM) in achieving its full potential.  
The Scheme was conceptualized to operationalize Skill India Mission by 
setting in motion the sub-Missions proposed under the NSDM. It is a US $ 
250 million (Rs.1,650 crore) World Bank Loan assisted Centrally Sponsored 
Scheme of the MSDE. The Scheme was made effective on 19th January, 
2018 with an initial implementation period till March, 2023, which has been 
extended till March, 2025.  The Committee further note that the World 
Bank has reviewed the project deliverables during Implementation 
Completion Mission (ICM) in March 2024 and submitted an Implementation 
Status and Results Report, in which they have rated the project's 
performance as 'Satisfactory’.  
The Committee have been apprised that the targets set for all the four 
Project Development Objectives (PDOs) under the Scheme have been 
achieved.  The Committee have also been apprised that the targets for all 
the Disbursement Linked Indicators (DLIs) have been achieved except for 

 
123 
 
DLI7, which is under verification by the Independent Verification Agency 
and is expected to be completed by March 2025. The Committee exhort the 
Ministry to make sincere efforts and ensure that verification of the 
remaining Disbursement Linked Indicator viz. DL17 is completed by 31st 
March, 2025.  Further, as informed by the Ministry, at present, there is no 
proposal to extend the Scheme beyond March, 2025 or introduce any other 
Scheme on similar lines. The Committee, therefore, recommend that an 
impact assessment of the Scheme be undertaken during 2025-26 and 
completed in a time bound manner. 
X. MISCELLANEOUS 
(i) Skill Development and upliftment of Tea Plantation Workers 
41. The Committee note that Assam, West Bengal, Tamil Nadu, Kerala and 
Karnataka are the major tea growing States. However, there is no job role 
exclusively related to Tea Plantation Workers under PMKVY 4.0. 
Considering the fact that tea plantations contribute significantly to 
employment and overall economic growth, the Committee recommend the 
Ministry to explore job role related skill training for Tea Plantation Workers 
under PMKVY 4.0 and set up JSSs in the remaining districts of these States 
so as to improve the income generation and livelihood of Tea Plantation 
Workers of the country.  
(ii) Review of National Policy for Skill Development and Entrepreneurship 
42.   The Committee note that the ‘Review of National Policy for Skill 
Development and Entrepreneurship’ Project was assigned to BCG India, 
which has submitted the draft National Policy Document in December 2024 
and the same is being reviewed in consultation with key stakeholders. The 
Committee call upon the Ministry to strengthen their coordination 
mechanism, analyse the views/suggestions of key stakeholders and 
complete the review exercise in a time bound manner so as to inter alia 

 
124 
 
enhance skill development ecosystem and foster lifelong learning to 
improve employability and meet the evolving needs of the economy. 
 
(iii) Setting up of 30 Skill India International Centres (SIICs) 
 
43. The Committee were apprised during evidence on 19.11.2024, that it is 
proposed to set up 30 Skill India International Centres (SIICs) to promote 
skill based International mobility. The Committee have now been apprised 
that while two SIICs have been established at Varanasi (Uttar Pradesh) and 
Bhubaneswar (Odisha), the work relating to setting up of additional 5 SIICs at 
Indian Institute of Entrepreneurship, Guwahati (Assam); NSTI, Bengaluru 
(Karnataka); NSTI, Ludhiana (Punjab); NSTI, Hyderabad (Telangana) and NSTI, 
Kanpur (Uttar Pradesh), is in advanced stage. The Committee desire that 
appropriate steps be taken on priority to ensure that the remaining Skill 
India International Centres are set up and made operational in a time bound 
manner so as to facilitate international workforce mobility opportunities for 
Indians and achieve the objective of making India the skill capital of the 
world. The Committee would like to be apprised of progress made in this 
regard.  
 
(iii) Action taken on the Observations/Recommendations of the 
Committee contained in their Third Report (18 LS) on Demands for 
Grants (2024-25) 
 
44. The Committee trust that the Ministry have taken appropriate action 
on the Observations/Recommendations of the Committee contained in their 

 
125 
 
Third Report on Demands for Grants (2024-25) of the Ministry, which was 
presented to both the Houses of Parliament on 16.12.2024.
